boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Sappony Church record (June 28, 1864) in the Richmond-Petersburg Campaign [June 1864-March 1865]. The Wilson-Kautz raid of June 22-July 1 contains three frozen records: Staunton River Bridge (VA113, June 25), Sappony Church (VA067, June 28) and Reams' Station (VA068, June 29). Hampton's report runs through the pursuit of June 29-30. Army-wide returns, raid-wide and multi-action loss totals, and the siege as a whole are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 'Divisions' and the live field zero. Wilson believed the only force barring him at Stony Creek was an infantry battalion and a remnant of W. H. F. Lee's cavalry, not over 1,000 men, until prisoners said Hampton's and Fitzhugh Lee's divisions had arrived; Hampton names Chambliss's and Young's brigades and 200 men of the Holcombe Legion.
claims.rationale: A pre-contact belief and partial formation lists; no count of either force at the church. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

open_questions: Chambliss's and Crawley's reports (not sent in, per Hampton), McIntosh's and Chapman's reports, Kautz's report (No. 280), Lee's June 29 dispatch (selected; cited under VA068) and Humphreys' raid passage (read, not selected) remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff, later commander of its Second Corps, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan; it relies on Meade's, Hancock's, Warren's, Burnside's, Parke's and Wilson's reports and quotes Lee's, Beauregard's and Gordon's despatches, so it is not independent of those families. Gillmore's, Meade's, Hancock's, Burnside's, Wilson's, Hampton's, Stannard's and Lee's papers, printed in Official Records Series I, Volumes XXXVI (Part 2), XL, XLII and XLVI (Part 1), are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; each volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Lee's telegrams largely relay subordinates' reports. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
